intent: The personal inbox moves to inbox.local.md, which checking out an older branch cannot overwrite
notes: After 2.40.0 made `.gator/inbox.md` personal and ignored (#104), checking out a branch from before that change overwrote the personal file with the old committed version, without warning: Git treats ignored files as disposable. Moving forward again then deleted it. Notes added since the file was last committed were lost (#113, reported by a user).

The personal inbox is now `.gator/inbox.local.md`, a path no commit has ever tracked, so no checkout, pull or merge can touch it. `gator init` (every session) and `gator update` move an untracked `.gator/inbox.md` there. An existing `inbox.local.md` with other content is never overwritten; the old file is kept beside it as `inbox.local.md.from-inbox-md` and Gator says so. While a branch still tracks `inbox.md`, Gator leaves it alone.

One ignore rule covers the personal file and any kept copy; `.gator/inbox.md` stays ignored, and a force-added `inbox.local.md` is untracked like the old file. New installs, `gator init`'s reading list, `gator pulse`, the Dashboard file list, the governance text and the layout contract use the new name.
Notes already overwritten this way cannot be recovered by Gator; Git never stored the ignored file.
Architect decision: rename to `.gator/inbox.local.md` (over a Git-private path, which editors and the Dashboard would not show).
